title: Add prompt-drift detection CI hook with per-suite thresholds
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: Add an automated prompt-drift gating step to our eval CI to catch regressions caused by prompt changes, model swaps, or tokenization differences before they reach production. This PR introduces a pluggable CI hook that runs configured prompt suites, computes a drift score (distributional and metric drop checks), and fails the pipeline when thresholds are exceeded. Key goals: (1) per-suite thresholds so teams can tune sensitivity, (2) clear failure reasons and artifact links, (3) minimal runtime overhead via cached embeddings/fixtures, (4) easy opt-in for new suites. Implementation summary: added a lightweight runner (ci/hooks/prompt_drift.py) that executes eval suites with a deterministic seed, computes baseline deltas against stored golden summaries under eval-harness/ci/goldens/, and emits a machine-readable report (JSON) and human summary in CI logs. A new config schema (eval_harness/configs/prompt_drift.yaml) allows per-suite thresholds, alert severity, and cache policy. Integrated the hook into our GitHub Actions eval workflow (ci/workflows/eval.yml) as an optional job guarded by label "prompt-drift" and by a feature flag. Tests: added unit tests for scoring and thresholds, and a small integration test that runs a toy suite in CI emulation. Linear: ENG-8271. Checklist: - [x] core runner and scoring implemented - [x] per-suite config and defaults - [x] CI workflow integration and gating - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and example golden - [x] smoke run on staging CI Notes: This description has links to the new docs page (docs/evals/prompt-drift.md) and the golden artifacts in the repo. Rollback plan: feature flag can be turned off and the CI job skipped; golden state is isolated under ci/goldens so reverting the config removes gating.

review_comments: Sofia Martinez: Worth documenting the statistical test used for detecting drift and examples of threshold tuning. Also asked for clearer failure messages so oncall can triage quickly.

Evan Park (author): Added a doc section that describes the two check types (metric-drop and distribution-shift) and suggested per-suite defaults; failure messages now include top-3 contributing prompts and artifact links.
Liam O'Connor: Requested caching for computed embeddings to reduce CI runtime; suggested a cache TTL config. Asked to ensure cache is optional and safe for PRs that modify prompts.
Evan Park: Implemented optional cache with TTL and safe invalidation for PRs touching prompt files; added tests for cache invalidation.
Priya Desai: Verified tests and asked for an example workflow snippet for teams to opt-in. Approves after docs addition.
release_notes: Adds a new CI prompt-drift check that can detect prompt/regression drift before merge. Per-suite thresholds are configurable. No breaking changes. Teams can opt-in via workflow labels or the feature flag.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for scoring edge cases and an integration smoke test that runs a small prompt suite against a deterministic toy model. CI run was executed on staging to validate runtimes and false-positive rates. See tests/test_prompt_drift_scoring.py for coverage.
